matches.rationale: No finding addresses the inflated dataset size claim in the abstract or misrepresentation of the DDL-12 dataset's image pairs.
No finding discusses the query-swapping inconsistency in cross-attention or any transformer mechanism details.

Finding 1 explicitly identifies the same asymmetric preprocessing protocol in Table 2, where the proposed method uses restoration pre-enhancement while competitors do not, matching the ground truth's experimental design flaw.
No finding mentions the exaggerated robustness or flexibility claims in the introduction.
No finding refers to the fabricated reference [8] (AutoDIR) or a non-existent paper being cited in related work.
No finding covers the missing ethical discussion in the conclusion.
No finding addresses the promotional, exaggerated language in the abstract about outperforming SOTA without caveats.
No finding discusses the unsubstantiated code availability claim in the abstract or its inconsistency with later sections.
No finding mentions the ambiguity in loss function application (symmetric vs. fused-only) in the method section.
No finding questions the small batch size and patch dimensions or their impact on training robustness.
No finding describes an overclaim of dominance when some metrics (e.g., EN, MUSIQ) are matched or surpassed by other methods.
No finding points to an overly optimistic framing of the degradation model in the conclusion while ignoring limitations.
No finding identifies the dubious 2025 references [38] and [43] or questions the temporal validity of the bibliography.
No finding mentions the absence of ethical discussion regarding dataset privacy or safety-critical applications in the experiments.
Finding 3 concerns efficiency metrics (Table 4), not the selective interpretation of performance metrics (MUSIQ) in Section 5.3, so it does not match this inconsistency.
